name: biped_mascot
doc: A front- or three-quarter-view standing mascot: hips, one torso bone, optional neck, head, optional clavicles, two arms (shoulder, elbow, wrist) and two legs (hip, knee, ankle).

{s} expands to each side in 'sides'. Side 'l' is the side whose source names carry an 'l'/'left' token; its outward arm swing is a negative local rotation when the arm hangs down on the left of the image (budget '+' = counter-clockwise, y up).

Bones: 'joint' names the joint at the bone's origin, 'tail' the joint it points at (no tail: the rig builder aims the bone at its own art, or keeps the parent's direction). 'parent' lists candidates, first one present wins.

Joint 'band': which layers bend there. 'both' = layers of the bone above and below the joint get the same ramp (elbows, knees, wrists, ankles: the two pieces must deform alike or the seam opens). 'lower' = only layers of the bone below the joint (a sleeve bends at the shoulder, the torso does not follow the arm). 'none' = rigid (a cartoon head does not bend at the neck).

Wrists are rigid: a mascot's hand piece usually carries the forearm too (the monkey's does), so a wrist band would take half of the short forearm from the elbow band and the elbow would fold from 40-70 deg instead of 90-120 (measured on the monkey, P2 step 2). The hand bone still exists for props.

Two bands on one layer share the distance between them equally (unless one overlaps the other, below). A band that reaches less than its half leaves the rest to the other (a short shoulder band gives the elbow's sleeve half room). A band never runs past a rigid joint down its lower bone (the elbow stops at the wrist).

Band shape (optional per joint): 'reach' {upper, lower} = halfwidths the band runs from the joint toward each bone (default 2 both ways, mesh.BAND_EXTENT); 'rows' = rows per half, one number or [upper, lower]; 'row_points' = interior points on every row of the band (the lean mesh otherwise keeps only a row's two outline points).

Elbows: reach 2.25 up the sleeve, 2 down the forearm (then clipped at the wrist), 4 rows on the forearm half, 3 points per row. The points cut the long fan triangles the lean mesh draws from the crook's outline vertex, which G2's single-triangle range caught first (a symmetric 2-halfwidth band without them held 58-78 deg on the monkey). The reach is a trade: art far off the axis needs a long ramp (a ramp of length e squeezes art y off the axis to ~1 - 0.56 (1 - cos(d/2)) - sin(d/2) y/e of its area), while G2's area sum, read over the joint's fixed window, loses more the further the ramp's middle reaches into it (P2 review R1: A1's 3.5 halfwidths read 94 deg at the monkey's right elbow over its own band and 80 over the window). Measured over the window (+ / - deg): synthetic arm 112/114 at 2, 114/114 at 2.25, 96/98 at 2.5, 92/92 at 3.5; monkey left elbow 88/84 at 2.25, 96/92 at 2.5 (its sleeve fans 1.7 halfwidths off the axis at the crook), right elbow 98/90 at 2.25, 104/82 at 2.5. One value cannot serve both of the monkey's arms: rigbuild --fit-reach fits each elbow by the budget (P2_REPORT review R1).

Helpers: a half-angle bone at the joint (SOTA 2 weights): the IR kind 'half_angle', which the Spine 4.2 emitter expands to a local rotate-only transform constraint with every other mix 0, ordered after IK.
IK: two-bone leg IK onto a target under root; the foot hangs from that target so a planted foot cannot slide (SOTA 5 M1). softness is a fraction of leg length, capped so the setup pose is unchanged.

IK knee direction ('knee'), from anatomy, never from the setup kink: 'outward' = a crouch moves each knee away from the body's midline (a front-view mascot's knees bend forward and outward, mirror-symmetric); 'facing' = along the character's facing (a side view; joints.json 'facing': 1 right, -1 left). A setup leg kinked the other way is straightened (its knee moved onto the hip-ankle line), because a two-bone IK would otherwise flip it at setup. A bool 'bend_positive' instead fixes Spine's bendPositive.

A planted foot is 100% foot below the ankle: the ankle band lies on the shin side of the ankle, so the whole boot stays on the ground and only the shin's art (and a boot shaft above the ankle) bends there.

'overlap': the band may run into the band of the joint above it on the same limb instead of sharing the bone between them; there its ramp splits whatever weight its upper bone holds (spinegen.weights CHAIN COMPOSITION; up to 3 influences: hips/thigh/helper or helper/shin/foot). Knees and planted ankles overlap: a deep crouch bends the knee ~100 deg and the ankle ~50 deg at once, and a mascot's short, flared calf cannot hold both ramps side by side (monkey, 0.10 H crouch: 24 folds shared, 0 overlapped; P2_REPORT A2). Knee: 2 halfwidths up the thigh, 1.5 down the calf; ankle: 3 halfwidths up the shin (one-sided when planted), each stopped at the next joint, so a planted ankle runs the whole calf. rigbuild --fit-crouch fits a leg's knee reach and ankle power to its art by the crouch grid's folds (the monkey's right leg: the knee down the whole calf and ankle power 0.9, its crouch grid 22 -> 0 folds; the synthetic flared calf of the tests keeps 1.5, which folds less there). 'power' (a band without a helper): its ramp is t ** power, steeper near the upper bone when > 1, near the lower bone when < 1; rigbuild --fit-crouch fits it per leg (the monkey's right ankle 0.9: its hem flares just above the ankle). A band above an overlap keeps the length its template asks for; with none it still stops at its half of the gap (the hip). 'compose' (overlap bands): 'upper' (default) = the band's ramp splits its upper bone's weight; 'row' = the band's own bone takes its ramp value of the whole row and the bones already there keep theirs, scaled by the rest (spinegen.weights CHAIN COMPOSITION). Ankles compose by row: in a crouch with the weight shifted onto one leg that ankle bends 50-67 deg, and art far off its axis (the monkey's right hem flares 93 px) needs the foot's weight to fall off evenly over the whole calf; split out of the shin's share it falls off up to 1.8x faster where the knee's ramp starts (monkey, depths 0.05-0.13 H x hips shifted -40..+40 px: 137 folds by 'upper' at 2.4 halfwidths, 22 by 'row' over the whole calf; P2_REPORT review R2).

match: token sets tried against source bone names (split at '_', '-', digits and camelCase; lower-cased); a source bone takes the first role in match_order with a set it contains. Unmatched source bones are carried over as accessories under their mapped parent.
